Theme 015 · Typography & graphic systems

Rubber Stamp & Riso Ink

Everything is printed on warm stock in two riso inks, teal and fluorescent coral, with slight misregistration, halftone dots and translucent overprints. Pulse works like a clerk with two rubber stamps: teal "✓ WATCHED" on every healthy slip, and one coral "HOLD — YOUR CALL" slammed onto the anomaly.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Plate pair — every hero word printed twice, teal and coral, multiply-blended and 4–6 px out of register.
  • Halftone disk — a dot screen in one ink, fading out radially, behind the mark and the CTA.
  • Rubber stamp — double-ruled frame, uppercase Manrope 800, distressed with a noise mask and a slight edge wobble.
  • Round seal — circular stamp with text on a path ("NOW WATCHING · 14 METRICS").
  • Inspection slip — small printed form per metric with a colored header rule; the anomaly slip is the large coral one.
  • Paper stock — warm off-white with grain; cards and slips cast soft, low shadows.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Stamp slam — scale 1.4 → 1 in 120 ms (power4.in) plus a two-frame 3 px shake; always on a kick or snare at 120 BPM.
  • Plate drift — the coral plate wanders 1–3 px on a 2 s sine loop (one bar), so printed words feel alive between hits.
  • Ghost lift — the stamp lifts 20 px and fades, leaving a 40% impression that fully inks in over 300 ms.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Stamps are the oldest symbol of "checked and approved", and two stamp colors make the split between routine and exception instant. Riso texture adds warmth to a product that otherwise lives in cold dashboards. Risk: the zine feel can undercut precision, so keep layouts rigid and numbers crisp.

Adapt to your product: turn each item your product checks (orders, PRs, invoices, leads) into a slip; stamp the routine ones in your brand color and give the exception its own loud stamp and a human-action stamp.

References: Studio 2AM — the risograph effect and ink misregistration
